1.why: verify-token compares the supplied code via timingSafeEqual against the token stored in the caller's own session and additionally requires recovery.real (the account email matched), so the code is bound to the requesting session/account.

2.why: False: each recovery token is a fresh 32-byte random value stored per-session and marked tokenConsumed after one successful use, so it cannot work for any other user or session.

3.why: True: password-update only sets recovery.passwordUpdated on the current session and contains no logic to invalidate other sessions, so any previously authenticated session remains valid until its 24h expiry.

4.why: The server only listens via Bun.serve with TLS cert/key and sets HSTS, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned to the latest version.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens are stored as plaintext hex in the in-memory session map rather than encrypted or hashed.

6.why: Delivery is simulated by returning testDeliveryToken in the API response and printing it into the page's Logs list and console, so the message channel does not guard the private token.

7.why: All inputs are strictly validated: email regex plus 254-char cap, token constrained to ^[a-f0-9]{64}$, MFA code to ^\d{6}$, password length/policy checks, and JSON body type/size limits.

8.why: The application performs no external redirects at all—every fetch is same-origin and CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none', so no unsafe redirect target exists.

9.why: All dynamic content, including simulated delivery messages, is inserted exclusively via textContent and scripts are restricted by a nonce-based CSP, so no user-supplied HTML or script can render.

10.why: False: the client explicitly writes the reset token and MFA code into the visible Logs UI element and browser console ('[delivery simulation] Reset token: ...').

11.why: The MFA secret '481516' is hardcoded in plaintext and an initial bcrypt password hash is embedded directly in the source, so secret codes are in the code even though passwords are bcrypt-hashed.

12.why: The system ships with a preset credential—a hardcoded initial passwordHash plus fixed account email—so a default credential effectively exists.

13.why: The allowed() rate limiter permits at most 5 attempts per 15-minute window per action/context/IP and then imposes a 15-minute block, returning 429.

14.why: Initiate returns the same generic 'If an account can use that address...' message and a token regardless of whether the email is real, though the bootstrap recoveryStage ('request' vs 'confirm-token') can subtly hint at account existence after a refresh.

15.why: The reset code is a 64-hex-character value from randomBytes(32) (CSPRNG), single-use and 15-minute-lived, bound to the requesting session and gated on the matching account email rather than an explicit user ID.
